 The Blue Road – Review | Netflix Series
 Posted by Karina "ScreamQueen" Adelgaard | Nov 20, 2026 | 4 min 
 THE BLUE ROAD on Netflix is a crime thriller series that immediately reminded me of both Se7en and Saw , with a touch of True Detective . The story is set in Japan and South Korea during the 2002 World Cup and is all about a disturbingly sinister serial killer. Read our The Blue Road series review here!
 THE BLUE ROAD is a Netflix series from Japan and South Korea (org. title: Puleungil ). With eight episodes, each around 45 minutes in runtime, this crime thriller series is extremely binge-worthy. From the opening scene, you’ll know that the serial killer in this Netflix series is among the most sinister in cinematic history.
 This Netflix series reminded me of Saw with that first scene, then the vibe became more  Se7en – inspired , before finally reminding me of True Detective as well. The storyline is all about the underworld and the darker parts of society. Both the villains and the victims of criminal activity.
 Continue reading our  The Blue Road  series review below. Find all eight episodes on Netflix now.
 Catching a serial killer in 2002
 The Blue Road plays out in 2002, during the soccer World Cup that took place in Japan and South Korea as a joint effort. The cooperation in this Netflix series, however, is all about catching the serial killer that has been leaving twisted and tormented bodies in both countries.
 I love how this storyline is set in 2002. Not just for the nostalgia, but also because it offers some challenges that we don’t have today. The internet is still in its early stages, social media is barely a thing, and your phone is used for phone calls and text messages. That’s it. In that sense, it’s the same setting as in The Body , which I also  adored .
 In  The Blue Road , we follow two detectives from South Korea and Japan, who join forces to catch a brutal serial killer. The killer has been leaving bodies in both countries. Of course, the killer is believed to be Japanese in South Korea, and Korean by the police in Japan. Isn’t that always the way it goes?!
 Fortunately, the two detectives working the case don’t care too much about the nationality of the killer. They just want to catch the perpetrator.
 A character-driven serial killer plot
 With this Netflix serial killer series being from South Korea and Japan, it’s hardly surprising that it features a very character-driven plot. What I love about it is how different the two detectives are, while being fairly quick to acknowledge that both have useful skills and methods.
 The comparison to  Se7en  is due both to the dark setting with sinister murders and  the two detectives. For me, the South Korean investigator reminded me of Morgan Freeman’s character in David Fincher’s iconic serial killer movie, while the Japanese cop was all Brad Pitt. A hothead who has his heart in the right place, but moves a little too fast at times.
 The casting of the lead characters in  The Blue Road  is spot-on. We have Son Sukku ( A Killer Paradox , Sense8 ) as the South Korean Kim Seok and Eita Nagayama ( Monster ) as the Japanese Inspector Inose. Also, you can look forward to some amazing supporting characters, who are also portrayed by familiar faces.
 A personal favorite of mine is Kim Shin-rock , who you should recognize from Colony , Hellbound , and Sweet Home . She is part of the criminal underworld in Japan, but works with other South Koreans. In other key roles, we get Jeong Jae-young ( Revolver ) and Choi Sung-eun ( Beyond Evil ).
 Watch  The Blue Road  on Netflix now
 The Blue Road is from director Han Jun-hee, who previously directed the Netflix series D.P. (2021-) and Weak Hero Class 1 (2022) . More recently, he directed Dead-End Job , which is another amazing Netflix genre series. Han Jun-hee also co-wrote this 2026 Netflix serial killer series with Cho Yu-jin ( The Witch ).
 The Netflix series is based on the 2002 Korean-Japanese webtoon “Blue Road” by Keishi Edogawa and Kwon Kaya. From the very beginning, there has been a lot of interest in this production. Now that I’ve watched it, I can easily understand why.
 It was selected for the On Screen section of the 31st Busan International Film Festival. There, three of its eight episodes were screened on October 7, 2026, which added further to the hype ahead of this global Netflix November release.
 If you like serial killer plots and recognize the gorgeous production quality and character-driven storytelling of South Korean (and some Japanese) productions, then you do not want to miss out on The Blue Road . I’m writing this review based on the first three episodes, but I will watch the rest as fast as I can. To avoid spoilers, and because I’m hooked on it.
 The Blue Road series premieres exclusively on Netflix on November 20, 2026.

 Plot
 In Tokyo, a disfigured body is discovered with a blood-inked message written in Korean. The shocking message leads Japanese police to uncover a disturbing truth that an identical murder had already taken place in Korea. With messages left in Korean and Japanese at crime scenes across two countries, the authorities launch a joint investigation to stop the serial killer operating across borders. The detectives from both countries follow a trail of mystery that stretches beyond Seoul and Tokyo.
